title: Review (Supported): on fresh seeds 5-6 a lone neural-field comet stays one body for 600 t at theta=0.5, and at theta=0.49 it grows into wave segments that fragment or wrap the domain; no binary fission of a compact comet
summary: c20's isolate.py on the sighting world (run to t=200, keep the median body, follow it alone for 600 t). theta=0.5: one body throughout on both seeds (seed 5: 36-44 px; seed 6: 88-91 px). theta=0.49: seed 5 grows into long travelling segments that break into 6 bodies of 33-462 px; seed 6 grows into one ~1000 px segment plus one 35 px piece. labkit on the default world (theta 0.5) seed 5: 14-60 bodies, 28 tracks travel >= 1 body length (max 40.5), 16 splits of which 3 persistent (generation 2): the population does split, which the isolation runs attribute to break-ups rather than to fission of a compact comet.

observations.D: negative replicated: isolation/iso_th0.5_s5.txt and _s6.txt: 1 body at every sample to +600; iso_th0.49_s5/s6: segments growing to 462-1016 px and fragmenting, no compact daughter pair

seeds_run.result: pass (single body at theta 0.5 is 88-91 px, larger than the finding's 32-42)

controls_run.D: isolation at theta 0.49 alongside theta 0.5 (isolation/), and the population run rerun/seed5

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at two of the five theta values; I did not trace the population's 3 persistent splits back to bar collisions myself. At theta 0.49 on seed 5 the isolation window already held 3 small pieces at +0.
